newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Esso Malaysia to explore for oil off Borneo.
newsitem.headline: Esso Malaysia to explore for oil off Borneo.

text.p: Esso Production Malaysia Inc, a division of Exxon, on Wednesday signed a contract to explore and develop oil offshore the Malaysian state of Sabah on Borneo island, officials said.

ESSO will hold an 80 percent interest in the two blocks awarded, while Petronas Carigali, the exploration subsidiary of Malaysia's state-owned oil firm Petronas, has the remaining 20 percent, Petronas President Massan Marican said.
The contracts incorporate a new "revenue over cost" formula, into Malaysia's standard Production Sharing Contract (PSC), Marican told reporters later.
Philip Dingle, chairman and CEO of Esso Companies in Malaysia, said the formula "is fairly new in the world".
"But it's not revolutionary, only more evolutionary," he told reporters. "As fields mature, we need new mechanisms to accommodate a changing geologic situation.
"We are quite happy with the mechanism that has been developed. It's quite a practical approach."
Neither Dingle nor Marican would give details about the formula, but industry sources say it would allow contractors to recover their costs more quickly.

In a speech at the signing ceremony, Dingle said the terms "take into account the level of exploration and production that has taken place in Malaysia's hydrocarbon basins and provide the framework needed to encourage the exploration and production of smaller oil and gas fields".
The two exploration and production contracts call for a total investment of more than 57 million ringgit ($23 million).

One is for Block SB302, covering an area of 4,721 square km about 80 km off Sabah. The block was previously awarded under 1985 PSC terms to a British Gas led consortium, which relinquished it last year.
The contract calls for Esso and Petronas Carigali to drill three wildcat wells to a combined minimum depth of 7,000 metres and do a detailed review of the block's hydrocarbon potential.
The contractors will make a minimum investment of 29.3 million ringgit. The exploration, development and production periods for the block are five, four and 20 years, respectively.

The second contract was for the deep-water Block H, about 135 km off Sabah and covering 8,054 sq km. The contractors would make a minimum investment of 28 million ringgit and agreed to drill three wildcat wells of a combined minimum depth of 7,500 metres. The exploration, development and production periods are seven, six and 25 years, respectively.
In a speech at the ceremony, Dingle said "it was a very significant day" for Esso.
It marks the company's return to upstream activities in Sabah after an absence of 11 years and Block H is the company's first deep-water contract in Malaysia, he said.
